topic.title: Evaluation in CI — golden sets, regression and quality gates

outcomes: Build a versioned golden dataset and deterministic evaluation harness for model/prompt candidates.
Measure task success, structured correctness, safety violations, latency and cost with explicit denominators.
Compare candidate and baseline on the exact same dataset and evaluator version.
Enforce quality, safety, latency, cost and non-regression thresholds as CI gates.
Persist immutable evaluation reports bound to model/prompt release bundle digests.
Separate deterministic checks, model-based judges, human review and production monitoring.
prerequisites: Stage 9 Topics 1–2: experiment tracking and model/prompt registry
Stage 5 RAG evaluation metrics, Python testing, JSON, GitHub Actions and release bundles

glossary.definition: A versioned set of representative inputs and expected properties used to compare candidate behavior.
One input with expected facts, structured schema, safety constraints and metadata.
A deterministic rule, reference-based metric, model judge or human rubric that scores an output.
A measurable decline against a declared baseline on the same dataset and evaluator.
A policy decision that blocks promotion when required metrics or evidence fail.
Evaluating baseline and candidate on identical cases so differences are attributable and comparable.
A model used to score outputs; it needs calibration and must not be the sole safety authority.
An immutable artifact binding candidate digest, dataset hash, evaluator version, metrics and gate outcomes.
A range expressing uncertainty in an estimated metric, especially on small samples.
A CI check that returns a failing exit code when a candidate does not satisfy policy.

explanation.problem: A model can compile, deploy and return plausible text while silently regressing on correctness, safety, latency or cost. Unit tests catch code defects, but AI behavior changes with model weights, prompts, tools, retrieval data and decoding settings. Evaluation must become a repeatable release gate, not a manual spot check.
explanation.plainLanguage:
Start with a golden dataset that represents real user intents, edge cases, difficult inputs, multilingual examples, safety cases and known failure modes. Give each case a stable ID, dataset version, source/provenance, expected facts or structured output, safety constraints and tags. Remove personal or secret data, obtain appropriate review rights and keep a held-out set to reduce overfitting. A golden set is a maintained product asset, not a random handful of easy examples.

Use deterministic evaluators wherever possible. Examples include exact schema validation, required-field checks, policy assertions, citation presence, allowed tool-call checks, forbidden phrase detection and deterministic reference matching. For open-ended language, use a calibrated rubric or model judge as one signal, but sample outputs for human review. An LLM judge can be biased, inconsistent or vulnerable to the same prompt injection as the candidate; it must not independently authorize high-impact actions.

Evaluate the candidate and baseline against the same dataset version and evaluator version. Report denominators, missing outputs, task success, precision/recall where applicable, safety violations, p50/p95 latency, token usage and cost. Never compare two models on different case subsets and call the result a fair regression test. Missing cases should fail the run or be explicitly marked as skipped under a reviewed policy.

Set release gates before running the candidate. A policy might require task success at least 90%, zero critical safety violations, p95 latency under 1.5 seconds, average cost below a budget, and no more than a two-percentage-point decline against baseline. Thresholds depend on use case and risk. High-impact workflows may require stronger safety checks and human review. Track sample size and uncertainty: a one-point change on ten cases is not strong evidence of improvement.

A single aggregate score can hide catastrophic failures. Keep safety as a separate hard gate, inspect per-category metrics, slice by language/intent/customer segment and report worst-case regressions. Prevent Simpson's paradox by comparing the same case IDs and segment weights. For stochastic models, repeat selected cases with controlled seeds or multiple trials and report variance; do not pretend one run is perfectly deterministic.

Bind each report to the exact model/prompt release bundle digest, golden dataset hash, evaluator version, policy version, runtime configuration and CI commit. Store raw case-level results securely with access controls and retention limits. Reports should be immutable: re-running a changed evaluator creates a new report ID. Never log secrets or raw sensitive user content unnecessarily.

In CI, build the candidate bundle, run fast deterministic tests, run golden-set evaluation, compare against the baseline, generate a machine-readable report and fail the pipeline if any hard gate fails. Attach the report as a build artifact and make the promotion workflow require the exact report hash. Expensive human review and large benchmark suites can run as separate pre-release or scheduled jobs, but a required release gate must not silently skip them.

Evaluation in CI is not production monitoring. CI estimates behavior on known cases; production telemetry detects drift, new intents, abuse, latency changes and distribution shifts. Feed reviewed incidents into future golden-set versions, but keep a protected holdout so the benchmark does not become a target that models memorize.
explanation.mentalModel: Version the golden set → run baseline and candidate on identical cases → score independent quality dimensions → compare against policy → persist report bound to bundle digest → block or allow promotion.
limitations: A golden dataset only represents what it contains; monitor production distribution and blind spots.
String matching is a teaching evaluator, not a semantic correctness proof.
LLM judges can be biased, unstable and prompt-injected; calibrate and supplement with human review.
Small samples have high uncertainty; report counts, slices and confidence intervals.
A passing CI score does not guarantee safe behavior for every user or input.
Evaluation reports must be privacy-aware and immutable; avoid storing raw sensitive outputs unnecessarily.
explanation.everydayAnalogy: A driving test uses the same route, rules and scoring rubric for every candidate. A driver is not passed because the car starts; they must meet safety, control and time requirements. If the route or rubric changes, scores are not directly comparable.
explanation.mathMadeSimple: Suppose a golden set has 100 cases. Baseline passes 92 and candidate passes 90, so success changes from 92% to 90%, a −2 percentage-point regression. If policy allows at most 1 point, the release is blocked. If one critical safety case fails, the safety gate can block even when overall success is 99%. A p95 latency of 1.8 seconds also fails a 1.5-second budget.
explanation.productionImpact: Version datasets and evaluators; bind reports to bundle hashes; use paired case IDs; keep safety separate from quality; set hard thresholds; capture cost/latency; persist immutable reports; fail CI closed; require report hash at promotion; and feed reviewed incidents into future benchmark versions.

useCase.scenario: A team proposes a new support-assistant model and prompt. CI runs the baseline and candidate on the same golden set, checks task success, forbidden content, p95 latency and cost, compares regression and stores a report linked to the release bundle.
constraints: Same case IDs and evaluator version for baseline/candidate comparison.
Missing outputs and critical safety failures fail closed.
Evaluation policy and dataset versions are immutable per run.
Raw outputs are minimized and access controlled.
Only a passing report bound to the exact bundle can satisfy promotion policy.
outputs: Immutable report hash and CI exit code
useCase.successMetric: The pipeline catches regressions before promotion and produces a reproducible report that can be traced to the exact release bundle.

dataFlow.purpose: Block release or authorize next governed step.

trustBoundaries: Golden data is reviewed, versioned and scrubbed; user content is not copied into fixtures without permission.
Candidate outputs and judge explanations are untrusted data, never policy instructions.
Evaluator code and policy versions are pinned and reviewed like production code.
Report store enforces tenant/project access and immutable run IDs.
Promotion verifies the report's bundle digest, dataset hash and policy version.
failurePaths: Missing candidate output: fail the case/run rather than silently shrinking denominator.
Critical forbidden output: fail hard safety gate regardless of aggregate score.
Dataset/evaluator mismatch: reject baseline comparison as invalid.
Metric regression: fail CI and attach case-level diff.
Judge disagreement: route to human review; never silently average away a critical issue.
Report ID reused with changed results: reject immutable report write.
CI evaluator unavailable: fail closed for required release jobs; do not treat timeout as pass.

Candidate passes 90 cases; p95 latency is above the budget.
The candidate exceeds the allowed regression and latency limit even though safety passes.
Save report with bundle digest, dataset hash, evaluator and policy version.

workedExample.expectedOutput: The candidate is not promoted. The report identifies the exact regression, latency failure, dataset and bundle digests so the team can reproduce and fix the issue.

failures.name: Golden-set denominator shrinks
failures.symptom: Candidate appears better because difficult cases were skipped.
failures.rootCause: Missing outputs are silently excluded from the score.
failures.recovery: Require exact case-ID coverage and fail on missing outputs.
failures.regressionTest: Remove one output and assert evaluation rejects the run.

failures.name: Safety regression hidden by average
failures.symptom: High task success masks a critical unsafe answer.
failures.rootCause: Safety is folded into one blended quality score.
failures.recovery: Keep safety as an independent hard gate.
failures.regressionTest: Inject a forbidden phrase and assert release fails even when task success remains high.

failures.name: Unfair baseline comparison
failures.symptom: Candidate delta looks better or worse due to changed cases or evaluator.
failures.rootCause: Baseline and candidate use different dataset/evaluator versions.
failures.recovery: Bind both reports to the same dataset hash and evaluator version.
failures.regressionTest: Different dataset hash or evaluator version is rejected.

failures.name: Latency or cost budget exceeded
failures.symptom: Quality improves but service becomes too slow or expensive.
failures.recovery: Add p95 latency and per-case cost hard thresholds.
failures.regressionTest: Inject latency and cost over budget and assert gate failure.

failures.name: Judge model is manipulated
failures.symptom: Judge gives high scores to unsafe or irrelevant outputs.
failures.rootCause: Judge is treated as a trusted policy engine.
failures.recovery: Use deterministic safety assertions and calibrated human-reviewed judge rubrics.
failures.regressionTest: Judge output cannot override a deterministic safety failure.

failures.name: Report rewritten after approval
failures.symptom: Same evaluation ID points to different results later.
failures.rootCause: Report store permits mutable run IDs.
failures.recovery: Hash canonical report and reject changed content under same tenant/run ID.
failures.regressionTest: Save same run ID with changed report and assert immutable conflict.

practice.guided: Take five golden cases and define required facts, forbidden outputs, evaluator version and minimum thresholds. Calculate baseline-to-candidate percentage-point delta.
practice.independent: Build a paired evaluation runner with missing-output checks, task success, safety, p95 latency, cost and a non-regression gate.
practice.realWorld: Add a required GitHub Actions job that evaluates a candidate model/prompt bundle, stores a report and blocks promotion when a hard gate fails.
practice.expertExtension: Add bootstrap confidence intervals, category slices, repeated stochastic trials, calibrated judge/human agreement, protected holdout sets and drift-driven dataset refresh.

scenarioQuiz.question: Why must baseline and candidate use the same case IDs?
options: To make the comparison paired and fair
scenarioQuiz.explanation: The same cases and evaluator make score deltas comparable.

scenarioQuiz.question: Candidate task success is 99%, but one critical safety violation occurs and policy allows zero. What happens?
options: Block on the independent safety gate
Ask the candidate model to approve itself
scenarioQuiz.explanation: Critical safety is a hard gate and cannot be averaged away.

scenarioQuiz.question: What should CI do when an output is missing for a golden case?
options: Fail or mark an explicitly reviewed skip
scenarioQuiz.explanation: Silent denominator changes invalidate the benchmark.

scenarioQuiz.question: What identifies the exact evaluation evidence used for promotion?
options: Bundle digest + dataset hash + evaluator/policy version + report hash
scenarioQuiz.explanation: The promotion step must verify the immutable report against the exact release candidate.

rubric.evidence: Stable case IDs, version/hash, coverage, privacy review and holdout policy.
Correct denominators, task success, safety, latency and cost.
Baseline and candidate use identical cases/evaluator and compute deltas correctly.
Hard thresholds fail closed and report actionable per-case evidence.
Report is bound to bundle digest and cannot be rewritten under same run ID.

evidence: Missing outputs and dataset/evaluator mismatch are rejected.
Safety, latency and cost gates are independent.
Candidate regression blocks CI as configured.
Report persistence is immutable and tenant scoped.

codeWalkthrough.explanation: Every golden case must have exactly one candidate result; silently skipping difficult examples invalidates the denominator.
A deterministic check is easy to reproduce, but substring matching is only a teaching proxy for semantic correctness.
A regression delta is meaningful only when both versions are evaluated against the same dataset and evaluator.
Keep safety as an independent hard gate so high average quality cannot hide a critical violation.
The report hash binds the decision evidence and prevents a run ID from being silently rewritten.
CI must fail closed: a blocked or incomplete required evaluation cannot be treated as successful promotion evidence.
